page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Baking soda
lines: carbonate. It is also called sodium
steps.why: The chemical name fixes which compound the common name means: the hydrogen carbonate of sodium, with one sodium ion for each hydrogen carbonate ion.
common_mistakes: Writing Na₂CO₃ for baking soda. That formula is sodium carbonate, the washing soda salt.
Leaving out the hydrogen and writing NaCO₃, which is not a real formula.
steps.memory_tip: Baking soda keeps its hydrogen: NaHCO₃.
steps.margin_note: Write the chemical name beside the formula.

steps.label: Washing soda
steps.why: Washing soda is the crystalline salt that holds ten water molecules. The same salt without that water is soda ash, so the ten water molecules are part of what the name means.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the ten water molecules. Washing soda is the decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.
Writing NaHCO₃ for washing soda. That formula is baking soda.
steps.memory_tip: Washing soda carries ten water molecules; baking soda carries none.
steps.margin_note: The ten water molecules are part of the formula.

insider_note: Write the chemical name with each formula: the two common names are close, and the name makes clear which salt you mean.
